Train 5, item 1b: tools/stress-tests.mjs must stop the current round on Ctrl-C.

Today each round runs in a detached process group and only the TIMEOUT path kills the group. Add SIGINT and SIGTERM handling for the stress runner itself:
- Track the active round child. On SIGINT/SIGTERM, kill the current round's process group (process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'), fallback child.kill('SIGKILL')), print a clear line like 'stress round <i>/<N>: interrupted by <SIGINT|SIGTERM>; killed the round process group', and exit 130 for SIGINT / 143 for SIGTERM (after the kill, no waiting on the child).
- If no round is active, exit with the same code immediately.
- Keep the timeout path, fail-fast, tails, round lines and env overrides unchanged. Clear the tracked child when a round finishes.
- For testing, allow an env override STRESS_TEST_COMMAND (a JSON array argv) to replace the default node --test command for a round; default stays exactly as today. This is test-only plumbing, do not use it in the normal path.
- Add tests/stress-interrupt.test.mjs: spawn tools/stress-tests.mjs with STRESS_TEST_COMMAND set to a long sleep/hang (e.g. ["node","-e","console.log(process.pid);setInterval(()=>{},1000)"]) and STRESS_ROUNDS=1; wait until the fake round's pid is printed; send SIGINT; assert the runner exits 130 within a few seconds, prints the interrupted line, and the fake round pid (and its group) is dead. Add the same check for SIGTERM -> 143 if cheap. Then a normal STRESS_ROUNDS=1 STRESS_CONCURRENCY=4 npm run test:stress must still pass.
Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/stress-interrupt.test.mjs; STRESS_ROUNDS=1 STRESS_CONCURRENCY=4 npm run test:stress. Report counts and any orphan check.
